name: Celluloses & Modified Celluloses
aliases: E460, E460(i), E460(ii), E461, E462, E463, E464, E465, E466, INS 467, E468, E469, cellulose, microcrystalline cellulose, cellulose gel, powdered cellulose, methyl cellulose, methylcellulose, ethyl cellulose, ethylcellulose, hydroxypropyl cellulose, hydroxypropyl methyl cellulose, HPMC, ethyl methyl cellulose, sodium carboxymethyl cellulose, carboxymethyl cellulose, CMC, cellulose gum, ethyl hydroxyethyl cellulose, cross-linked sodium carboxymethyl cellulose, enzymatically hydrolysed carboxymethyl cellulose
what_is: A family of cellulose and modified-cellulose texturisers. The current EU list includes E460–E466 and E468–E469; JECFA also recognises ethyl hydroxyethyl cellulose as INS 467.
why_botia: Food-grade cellulose can be obtained from wood pulp or other plant fibres and is used as a thickener, stabiliser or anti-caking agent — for example, it helps keep grated cheese from clumping. Cellulose E460 is not digested as a nutrient: it acts mainly as fibre and much of it is excreted in the faeces. Derivatives such as cellulose gum, CMC or HPMC may also appear on the label; they are not the same substance. JECFA did not set a numerical limit for cellulose, nor for the group of modified celluloses it evaluated.
can_1: Detect the current EU cellulose codes and common names, plus INS 467 where that international identifier is actually declared.
can_2: Show the texture and numbering context while distinguishing EU E-numbers from an INS identifier used outside the EU list.
